title: NBA adds Novig as its fourth prediction market partner - The Athletic
summary: The NBA just brought Novig on as its fourth official prediction market partner, expanding the league's betting infrastructure beyond traditional sportsbooks. This signals serious mainstream acceptance of prediction markets and probably means more sports leagues will follow suit once they see the data flow and engagement these platforms generate.

title: Trump admin orders Kalshi to halt wagers on what words Trump will say
summary: The Trump administration ordered Kalshi, a leading prediction market platform, to stop offering contracts that bet on specific words or phrases the president will use in speeches or statements. It's the most direct regulatory attack yet on prediction markets and signals the administration views certain types of political wagering as off-limits.

title: Kalshi Turns to Compute Desk in Renewed Push for GPU Futures
summary: Kalshi, the regulated futures exchange, is partnering with Compute Desk to launch GPU futures contracts that let traders bet on graphics processor prices and availability. This fills a gap in the prediction market ecosystem since GPU costs directly move crypto mining profitability, AI infrastructure spend, and semiconductor supply chain bets.

title: How much will Anthropic be worth at IPO? New platforms like Polymarket offer early clues
summary: Prediction markets are pricing Anthropic's eventual IPO valuation, giving us real-time crowd estimates on what the AI darling might be worth when it goes public. For bettors, these prices reveal where smart money actually sits versus the hype cycle, and they tend to be eerily accurate when it matters.

title: Kyle Kuzma: ‘It’s BS’ NFL Won’t Let Players Invest in Prediction Markets
summary: Kyle Kuzma is calling out the NFL's ban on players investing in prediction markets, arguing the league's restrictions are outdated and nonsensical. If the association's loudest star players keep pushing back, the NFL could eventually crack under pressure and open up another $500M+ addressable market of high-net-worth degenerates looking to park money somewhere.

title: Polymarket US brings 15-minute trading to oil and natural gas
summary: Polymarket is launching a US version with 15-minute expiration contracts on energy commodities, letting traders bet on oil and gas price movements with the kind of speed you'd normally find in crypto or stock options. Speed-based trading creates the conditions for more sophisticated players to arbitrage inefficiencies and volatility, which probably means tighter spreads and deeper liquidity for everyone else willing to place a bet.

title: How to Play META Stock as Meta Platforms Tests a New Prediction Markets App
summary: Meta is building its own prediction markets app, which means the company that owns Facebook and Instagram is finally getting serious about monetizing amateur forecasters. If they nail the execution, they're about to become the dominant player in a space that's been fragmented between Polymarket, PredictIt, and a bunch of sketchy offshore sites.

title: Prediction market versus poll performance in the 2026 midterms
summary: Prediction markets are already diverging from traditional polls on 2026 midterm outcomes, with bettors pricing in scenarios that pollsters haven't caught up to yet. If markets keep outperforming polls like they did in recent cycles, that's a giant middle finger to the entire polling industry and a validation that real money beats random samples every time.

title: Kalshi bets on Martha Stewart to clean up its image
summary: Kalshi, the prediction market platform that got nuked by regulators last year, is apparently trying to rebrand itself by partnering with Martha Stewart, betting her homemaking empire cachet can rehabilitate its image. If it works, it signals that prediction markets are finally shedding their casino stigma and moving toward mainstream legitimacy, which would actually matter for whether these platforms survive the next regulatory wave.

title: CFTC nominee questions public benefit of prediction markets as legal fight grows
summary: The CFTC's incoming leadership is questioning whether prediction markets actually benefit the public, even as the agency fights legal battles over its authority to regulate them. If skepticism at the top sticks, don't expect aggressive enforcement against gray-market platforms anytime soon.

title: Kalshi loses bid to prevent Maryland from policing prediction market
summary: Kalshi, the leading US prediction market platform, failed to block Maryland from enforcing state gambling regulations against its operations. The loss opens the door for other states to regulate prediction markets as gambling rather than financial derivatives, potentially fragmenting the market and forcing operators to pick which jurisdictions they'll serve.

title: Kalshi halts trading on Trump's speeches
summary: Kalshi, the regulated prediction market platform, stopped accepting bets on whether Trump will give specific speeches, likely due to regulatory pressure or concerns about market manipulation. This signals that even approved prediction markets face hard limits on what they can actually trade, which matters if you're betting there.

title: Georgia Prediction Markets: Best Promos and Apps in GA
summary: Georgia just legalized sports betting, and the apps are already running sign-up bonus wars to grab market share. Early movers who lock in the best promos could save hundreds before the state's regulatory dust settles.

title: Kyrie Irving NBA Trade Market on Kalshi Remains Low Despite Rumors
summary: Kyrie Irving's name keeps floating around the trade rumor mill, but prediction market traders on Kalshi aren't exactly rushing to bet on a deal happening. That gap between gossip and actual market conviction usually signals either the rumors are overblown or the market is sleeping on a real opportunity.

title: Are Prediction Markets the Future of Finance?
summary: Prediction markets are getting pitched as the next big thing in financial infrastructure, with backers claiming they'll eventually replace traditional forecasting methods. If true, that means serious money flows into volume and liquidity for the platforms that nail user experience and regulatory compliance first.

title: Polymarket Indicates 29% Chance Anthropic’s Market Cap Lands Above $1.5 Trillion
summary: Polymarket traders are betting there's a 29% shot Anthropic reaches a $1.5T valuation, a figure that would put the AI startup in rarefied air alongside only Apple, Saudi Aramco, and Microsoft. That low probability reflects deep skepticism about whether Claude can actually convert hype into the kind of sustained revenue dominance needed to justify a valuation 3x higher than current unicorn pricing.

title: Another U.S. appellate court goes against Kalshi, building the industry's legal headwinds
summary: A federal appeals court just sided against Kalshi, the prediction market platform trying to get regulators off its back, adding another legal loss to its mounting pile. If courts keep ruling this way, the entire U.S. prediction market industry could stay locked out of mainstream adoption for years.

title: Kalshi files to voluntarily dismiss its lawsuit against Louisiana
summary: Kalshi, the CFTC-approved prediction market platform, is dropping its legal challenge against Louisiana's attempt to block the platform from operating in the state. The retreat signals that prediction markets still face real regulatory headwinds, even with federal blessing, and suggests other states will feel emboldened to push back without fear of costly litigation.

title: Zohran Mamdani says prediction markets are troubling and 'degrade so much of life'
summary: A New York state legislator is arguing that prediction markets commodify human outcomes in ways that are fundamentally corrosive to society. The comment signals growing political pushback that could translate into actual regulatory constraints on the industry just as it's gaining mainstream adoption.

title: Polymarket Founder Says Trump Jr.’s Involvement Is ‘Heavily Overblown’
summary: Polymarket's founder is pushing back on claims that Don Trump Jr. has significant influence over the platform's operations and decision-making. The clarification matters because regulatory scrutiny of prediction markets often hinges on perceived conflicts of interest, and any real or imagined political entanglement could invite unwanted attention from lawmakers already skeptical of crypto betting platforms.

title: Kalshi's Quintenz says insider trading is 'just easier to see' in prediction markets than stocks
summary: Kalshi's CEO argues that insider trading in prediction markets isn't uniquely worse than stocks, just more transparent when it happens. If regulators buy this framing, it could become much harder to justify cracking down on suspicious trading patterns that currently get flagged instantly.

title: How to Read Prediction-Market Odds in a News Headline
summary: Prediction markets are becoming mainstream enough that financial media now needs a translation guide for how to actually interpret the odds being quoted. If you're trying to arbitrage headlines against real market prices, you're already losing money to people who know what a 35% implied probability actually means.

title: Coinbase Eyes In-House Prediction Markets in First Half 2027
summary: Coinbase is building its own prediction markets platform and plans to launch it in the first half of 2027. If they actually ship it, we're looking at a major liquidity inflow to onchain prediction markets from one of crypto's largest retail gateways.

title: Michigan Forced Polymarket to Retreat. Did the State Expose Prediction Markets' Weak Spot?
summary: Michigan's regulators forced Polymarket to block residents from using their platform, testing whether states can weaponize gambling laws to crush prediction markets before they go mainstream. If other states follow suit, we're looking at a patchwork of regional bans that could balkanize the entire industry before it ever gets legitimacy.

title: Kalshi Asks States for Help in Restricting Problem Gamblers
summary: Kalshi, the CFTC-approved prediction market platform, is pushing state regulators to implement restrictions on problem gamblers to head off the inevitable crackdown that comes when politicians notice people losing rent money on event outcomes. It's a smart play to establish the guardrails themselves before someone else mandates them from above, though it also signals the prediction market industry knows its fragile regulatory window is closing fast.

title: Polymarket code “SILIVE” enhances $25 referral promo for Celtics-Nuggets
summary: Polymarket just dropped a referral code that bumps their standard $25 bonus to something sweeter, timed perfectly around a marquee NBA matchup between the Celtics and Nuggets. It's the kind of promotional judo that prediction market platforms use to acquire users when eyeballs are already glued to major sporting events.

title: ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Prediction Markets: Ezra Frech Favorite for Finale
summary: Ezra Frech, the Paralympic athlete turned reality TV competitor, is the betting favorite to win this season of Dancing With the Stars. His odds advantage suggests the market's pricing in both his athletic coordination and the sympathy bias that typically propels athlete contestants toward finale appearances.

title: Kalshi Asks States for Help in Restricting Problem Gamblers
summary: Kalshi's lobbying states to implement tighter restrictions on problem gamblers, essentially asking regulators to do the heavy lifting on consumer protection so the platform doesn't have to. If states actually follow through, prediction market operators face higher compliance costs and a smaller addressable market, but also get to point at "responsible gambling" measures when regulators come knocking.

title: Polymarket upgrades new $25 referral code “OREGON” for Jazz-Lakers NBA
summary: Polymarket rolled out a $25 referral bonus using code "OREGON" ahead of the Jazz-Lakers game, signaling the platform's bet on NBA content to drive user acquisition. Expect prediction market platforms to weaponize sports events as onramps now that crypto betting's regulatory uncertainty has cleared enough to justify marketing spend.

title: Video: Executives Discuss the Line Between Prediction Markets and Gambling
summary: Executives are apparently drawing lines in the sand between prediction markets (legitimate!) and gambling (sketchy!), which means the regulatory conversation is heating up. If they nail a legal distinction, it could unlock billions in mainstream money that's currently sitting on the sidelines waiting for official permission.
